newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert cautiously upbeat on 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert cautiously upbeat on 1997 profit.

text.p: The chairman of Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV said on Thursday he was "cautiously optimistic" about prospects for 1997 after profit slid in 1996.

"We are looking ahead to 1997 with confidence. It is our firm conviction that, barring major unforeseen developments, Bekaert will take a good step forward on the road to higher profitability this year," Baron Jean-Charles Velge told a news conference on 1996 results.

Despite a capital gain of 2.31 billion Belgian francs on the sale of shares in Japan's BMA, profit fell to 2.28 billion francs in 1996 from 3.18 billion in 1995 as slow demand for its main products and a slump in prices hit the group.
Bekaert announced in December a two-year restructuring plan to cut capacity at and restructure a number of European plants.

Chief executive officer Raf Decaluwe said this programme would have a "significant" effect on profitability in the coming years but only a modest impact on 1997. "We should start reaping the full benefits from 1999."

Decaluwe said 1997 had started with plants around the world operating at "reasonable capacity" but Bekaert was carrying the burden of lower steel cord prices. The start of the year was also marred by the flooding of a plant in Brazil.
"Despite these facts, I am strongly convinced that for the full year 1997, maybe not yet in the first half,...Bekaert expects to make progress towards higher profitability," he said.
